Can the Exact Derivatives of the Criterion Be Computed Here?

Source: R/outer_gradient.R
outer_gradient_ok.Rd

Returns TRUE when the exact gradient of the marginal criterion in the hyperparameters under estimation (order = 1), or the exact gradient and Hessian (order = 2), can be assembled for the model.

Usage

outer_gradient_ok(spec, design, idx, method, order = 1L, gamma = FALSE)

Arguments

spec

A StatmodSpec().

design

The design.

idx

The outer index, from outer_hyper_index().

method

An OuterMethod().

order

1 for the gradient, 2 for the Hessian as well.

gamma

TRUE where the outer vector also carries coefficients that the criterion estimates (marginal_coords()), so an empty index is not a reason to return FALSE.

Value

TRUE or FALSE.

Details

The family must carry the derivatives that the order needs (order_available()): the third derivative of the log-likelihood for the gradient and the fourth for the Hessian.

For the information, \(K\) enters the criterion through its determinant, so the gradient needs \(\partial K/\partial\beta\). With the observed information that is the third derivative of the log-likelihood in the link-scale predictors. With the expected information it is the derivative in the predictors of \(-E[\ell'']\), which is not \(-E[\ell''']\). That derivative is supplied by distributions7::distrib_dexpected_hessian(), and the expected route is admitted when the family returns it (expected_deriv_ok()). At order 2 the expected route is admitted only for reml() and ml(), for a model without a block that moves with its coefficients and without a structural term, and for a family that returns distributions7::distrib_d2expected_hessian() (expected_deriv2_ok()). The expected route is not admitted at either order where a penalty covers the parameters of a structural term, because the criterion is then assembled from the observed joint curvature.

For structural terms, a term of the likelihood shape (regime() and the marginal break-point term) has no exact derivatives at either order. For a term of the filter shape, order 2 requires a penalty over the term's own parameters and a term that implements modelterms7::term_fourth(). Where a penalty covers the term's parameters, the term must also implement modelterms7::term_third().

For moving blocks, a block that moves with its coefficients (nl(), seg(), jump() and jseg()) is admitted at order 1 on either route and at order 2 on the observed route. Its contribution is read from the term (u_refresh(), mode_curvature()) and is never differenced.

For penalties, \(\partial S/\partial\theta\) and its second derivative are given by the generics of penalties7 (penalties7::penalty_dhessian(), penalties7::penalty_d2hessian() and penalties7::penalty_dcross()). The function calls the derivative methods of a penalty at probe values and reads an error as a penalty that does not supply them, so that a penalty is admitted according to what its methods return and not according to its class. The check has two parts. Every penalized unit of the model is examined, because the movement of the mode reaches the determinant through each penalty whose Hessian moves with the coefficients (a Student t prior, for instance). A penalty for which penalties7::beta_quadratic() returns TRUE passes, and so does a penalty with a kink (a lasso, a SCAD or an MCP). Any other penalty must supply penalties7::penalty_dhessian_beta(), and a mixed covariance class of this kind is not admitted. Beside a structural term such a penalty is not admitted at order 2. The second part examines, with penalty_answers(), the penalty of every term that owns a hyperparameter under estimation, and for a hyperparameter shared by several terms the penalty of each of them. A penalty with a kink does not remove the exact derivatives of the other hyperparameters, because its own hyperparameters are left out of the outer index.

See also

statmod_marginal_grad()
